# Class 7 biology, ~2 minutes, written by Claude for F-014 S3 (processes). Expect: a content slide on photosynthesis;
# "let me show you how photosynthesis happens in a leaf" opens simulation mode (plant, Sun, five steps drawn, unnamed,
# the word equation as empty boxes); each step said moves the stage and fills its term; respiration is added only when
# said; "artificial photosynthesis" is a trap; "let's get back to the slides" ends the mode with a recap; then the
# slides go on (importance of plants). No numbers.
@setup subject=Biology grade=7 topic="Photosynthesis"

Good morning everyone. Today we are going to learn how green plants make their own food.
[pause 1]
This process is called photosynthesis. Photo means light and synthesis means putting together.
It takes place mainly in the leaves, in the green parts that contain chlorophyll.
[pause 1.5]
Let me show you how photosynthesis happens in a leaf.
First, chlorophyll absorbs sunlight. This light energy drives the whole process.
Water is absorbed by the roots and travels up the stem to the leaf.
Carbon dioxide enters the leaf through tiny pores called stomata.
[pause 1]
Inside the leaf, water and carbon dioxide combine and glucose is made.
Oxygen is released into the air through the stomata as a by-product.
[pause 1]
So the word equation is: carbon dioxide plus water, in the presence of light and chlorophyll, gives glucose plus oxygen.
Respiration is the reverse: glucose and oxygen give carbon dioxide and water, and energy is released.
[pause 1]
Scientists are also working on artificial photosynthesis to make solar fuels, but that happens in a lab.
[pause 1]
Okay, let's get back to the slides.
[pause 1]
Plants are the source of all our food, directly or indirectly.
They also keep the oxygen in the air that every animal breathes.
